Declan Walsh, 23, was arrested at his home in Stockport, Greater Manchester, on suspicion of controlling and coercive behaviour in March 2023. title: Legally Blonde at 25: Lawyers inspired by Reese Witherspoon's Elle Woods

evidence_packet.title: Legally Blonde at 25: Lawyers inspired by Reese Witherspoon's Elle Woods
evidence_packet.lead: Twenty five years after the release of Legally Blonde in the UK, lawyers discuss how the film inspired them
evidence_packet.summary: Twenty five years after the release of Legally Blonde in the UK, lawyers discuss how the film inspired them
evidence_packet.evidence_text: It has been 25 years since Elle Woods stomped her 'last season Prada shoes' across UK screens in Legally Blonde The film, which was released 25 years ago today, sees Woods played by Reese Witherspoon , enrol in Harvard Law School after her boyfriend dumps her for not being serious enough. The film went on to inspire generations of would-be lawyers and solicitors A quarter of a century later, women now outnumber men in the legal industry. And while "the Legally Blonde effect" may not be the sole reason for the boost, lawyers say it has not hurt the cause "It definitely inspired the kind of lawyer I wanted to be," trainee solicitor Olivia Holder said Olivia, who works for Manchester-based Express Solicitors, said she believes people's access to justice can improve when solicitors are free to be themselves "I love to wear pink, I've got a pink sparkly car and I didn't have to give up any of that to be taken seriously in the legal profession," she said

Ending rough sleeping was one of Andy Burnham's first promises when he entered Downing Street, announcing a £442m package to provide emergency accommodation and practical support. evidence_packet.summary: Ali and Fiona Wilshaw have estimated a loss of £50k as they shut to clear up after the storm
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Two sisters have spoken of the "catastrophic" £50,000 impact Storm Boelo caused to their farm Ali and Fiona Wilshaw, who run Bates Farm in Risley, Warrington, Cheshire, were expecting to welcome about 1,000 cars for pumpkin picking on Sunday, but were instead forced to cancel their event as instead they cleared up the destruction left by heavy rain and 50mph (80km/h) wind The impact from the storm had been "pretty unprecedented," Ali said, adding that it had been a sleepless night "We were up at 05:00 GMT doing a site tour of the destruction. We've got a marquee and a fair few gazebos from the food vendors, which are absolutely just obliterated." The sisters have been running Bates Farm since their father, Michael, died in October 2023 Speaking to the BBC in 2024, shortly after taking over the farm, Fiona said they had a lot to get their heads round but their father, who ran the farm for 30 years before he died of cancer, helped them as much as he could even when he was poorly

evidence_packet.title: Wythenshawe 100: Cabaret club on Europe's biggest council estate
evidence_packet.lead: The Golden Garter opened its doors in the Wythenshawe area of Manchester in 1968 and attracted huge stars
evidence_packet.summary: The Golden Garter opened its doors in the Wythenshawe area of Manchester in 1968 and attracted huge stars
evidence_packet.evidence_text: When the Golden Garter cabaret club opened its doors for the first time in October 1968, TV legend Sir Bruce Forsyth was the first name on the door Situated on a council estate in the Wythenshawe area of Manchester, people travelled from far and wide to enjoy shows at the 1,400-capacity venue From music stars Dusty Springfield, Roy Orbison and Eartha Kitt to comedians Tommy Cooper and Ronnie Corbett, there was never a shortage of acts wanting to appear "I think Dusty Springfield was the big highlight for me," said 79-year-old John Orchard, who was a pianist for Shep's Banjo Boys from 1969 to 1972 "She was my favourite singer in the 1960s and all of a sudden there she is at the Golden Garter "This is a nightclub in Wythenshawe under the flight path of the Ringway airport (now known as Manchester Airport) in the middle of the biggest council estate in Europe

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Families 'devastated' as Stretford school closure announced - BBC News Image caption, Sue Green says she does not want to move her daughter before the school closes By Haider Saleem Reporting from Greater Manchester Published 23 October 2026 Families have been left "absolutely devastated" by a decision to close a primary school in Greater Manchester. St Teresa's RC Primary School in Firwsood, Trafford, will close down in August 2027. One mother told the BBC she feared she might not be able to get a place for her daughter at another local Roman Catholic school. The council said falling pupil numbers had made the school's finances unsustainable. St Teresa's is a state-funded school and its budget is managed by its governing body. The Roman Catholic Diocese of Salford owns the site and has a role in its governance, but Trafford Council oversees its finances, and made the decision to close it. Council documents show St Teresa's had 109 pupils in July. Of those, 21 had since left to attend secondary school, while 51 secured places at other primary schools for September. With two new reception pupils joining, the school had 39 children on its roll by the time of the council's October report. The council estimated that 24 pupils would need to move to another primary school when St Teresa's closes, with the remaining 15 moving on to secondary school. Image caption, Helen fears she may struggle to secure a place at another nearby Catholic school for her daughter Parents and teachers said they believed the proposed closure encouraged families to move their children before councillors had reached a final decision. evidence_packet.evidence_text: It has been 25 years since Elle Woods stomped her 'last season Prada shoes' across UK screens in Legally Blonde The film, which was released 25 years ago today, sees Woods played by Reese Witherspoon , enrol in Harvard Law School after her boyfriend dumps her for not being serious enough. The film went on to inspire generations of would-be lawyers and solicitors A quarter of a century later, women now outnumber men in the legal industry. And while "the Legally Blonde effect" may not be the sole reason for the boost, lawyers say it has not hurt the cause "It definitely inspired the kind of lawyer I wanted to be," trainee solicitor Olivia Holder said Olivia, who works for Manchester-based Express Solicitors, said she believes people's access to justice can improve when solicitors are free to be themselves "I love to wear pink, I've got a pink sparkly car and I didn't have to give up any of that to be taken seriously in the legal profession," she said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing estate close to Manchester To turn his proposal into a reality, Ernest and Shena Simon bought Wythenshawe Hall from Robert Henry Grenville Tatton in 1926, which they donated to the city's corporation (now known as the council) The idea was that people could be rehoused away from industrial Manchester into what became known as the "Garden City" To celebrate 100 years, BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people from the area about what Wythenshawe means to them

evidence_packet.evidence_text: When the Golden Garter cabaret club opened its doors for the first time in October 1968, TV legend Sir Bruce Forsyth was the first name on the door Situated on a council estate in the Wythenshawe area of Manchester, people travelled from far and wide to enjoy shows at the 1,400-capacity venue From music stars Dusty Springfield, Roy Orbison and Eartha Kitt to comedians Tommy Cooper and Ronnie Corbett, there was never a shortage of acts wanting to appear "I think Dusty Springfield was the big highlight for me," said 79-year-old John Orchard, who was a pianist for Shep's Banjo Boys from 1969 to 1972 "She was my favourite singer in the 1960s and all of a sudden there she is at the Golden Garter "This is a nightclub in Wythenshawe under the flight path of the Ringway airport (now known as Manchester Airport) in the middle of the biggest council estate in Europe

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Everything heard in second week in the trial of a man accused of murdering Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins WARNING: Graphic details. Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering Michael Mullins View 9 Images Add to preferred sources New Simon Richardson, 35, struck Mr Mullins in his Volvo in Altrincham in April, at the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane, a jury was told. The 56-year-old was making his way home to Northwich from work, it was said It is alleged that Mr Richardson failed to properly observe the junction, 'flying straight through the give-way markers', before hitting Mr Mullins Minshull Street Crown Court heard that Mr Richardson 'put his foot down', as Mr Mullins was trapped under the car, while his damaged bike was left in the road He was dragged under the wheels of the car for 1.3 miles - 2.2km - before dying at the roadside on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm, it was said. Prosecutors allege that Mr Richardson later stopped, got out of the car and made 'concerted physical efforts' to try and pull Mr Mullins out from He then carried on driving, veering 'sharply and deliberately' from side to side and mounting a grass verge. Witnesses followed a trail of blood in the road before finding Mr Mullins fatally injured. He was pronounced dead at the scene

That is a recognised torture method' Former Tameside Mayor John Sullivan claims overnight M67 diversions for the £228m Mottram bypass project are sending 400 HGVs a night past his Hyde home - shaking b Add to preferred sources News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 17:56, 25 Oct 2026 Updated 06:21, 26 Oct 2026 Houses shake and residents are being kept up by lorries crashing over potholes in Mottram, according to one local John Sullivan says he’s not had a good night’s sleep since July, thanks to a diversion on the A57 link roads project. The scheme, also known as the Mottram bypass, has been designed to reduce congestion and improve journey times and reliability across the Pennines The A57 is a major connecting road between Manchester and Sheffield, which has been marred by congestion for years. The bypass was a ‘pie in the sky’ idea for more than 60 years, until spades finally went in the ground last year The current stage of roadworks is to allow the construction of a flyover from Hattersley roundabout to loop around Mottram village, go under Roe Cross, down to Mottram Moor and beyond towards Woolley Lane - ending at Woolley Bridge This progress on the scheme hasn’t made life easy for those that live nearby. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Councillor Pat Karney 'I couldn't deal with fire in my mouth': How losing his mum inspired Pat Karney's crusade to ban smoking Following the death of Cllr Pat Karney aged 78, John Scheerhout examines the personal tragedy that drove one of his greatest Add to preferred sources News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 17:21, 25 Oct 2026 Updated 06:22, 26 Oct 2026 Pat Karney watched his beloved mother Mary die of smoking-related illness. The late Labour veteran possessed an ingrained sense of public duty but perhaps it was this intens For years before smoking in pubs and restaurants was eventually outlawed in England in 2007, he was the passionate leader for a campaign to make Manchester smoke-free. Of course, he believed his adopted home city of Manchester should always be first His late mother had been seduced into addiction by images of the glamorous Hollywood greats, puffing away on the silver screen. So in 2004 he resolved to do something about a public health crisis which was blighting Manchester more than anywhere else in the country He had tried smoking at London School of Economics where he got a BSc in politics and economics and even tried a joint on a trip to Amsterdam but disliked it immediately. He admitted he 'couldn't deal with having a fire in my mouth' His campaigning went through many ups and downs but ended in victory, and probably helped to save lives. He died earlier this month, aged 78

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Ryanair flight from Spain to Manchester declares emergency at 12,000ft The flight from Seville declared an emergency shortly before landing at Manchester Airport Add to preferred sources News Olivia Beeson UK & World News Reporter a A Ryanair flight travelling from Spain to Manchester declared an emergency after a passenger fell ill on board The aircraft took off from Seville and was headed for Manchester Airport when the emergency code was transmitted by the crew on Sunday evening (October 25). The Boeing 737-800 flight RYR56QH issued the 7700 squawk code approximately 20 minutes before touching down at the airport The code indicates a general emergency, and it has since been confirmed that a passenger had taken ill during the journey. The flight landed safely at Manchester Airport , where medical crews were on hand to meet the plane and assist the unwell passenger, reports the Mirror The aircraft had been scheduled to depart Seville at 8.20pm, but did not take off until 9.33pm local time. According to Flight Radar, the plane touched down in Manchester at 11.30pm View 2 Images The emergency was declared just before landing (Image: Squawk)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Unseen pictures of 1930s from Manchester's Ritz to Rochdale 'Riviera' From Rochdale's lost "Norden Riviera" lido to an almost deserted East Lancashire Road, a remarkable new book featuring 600 unseen 1930s archive photographs captures Greater Manchest Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 05:53, 26 Oct 2026 Storm clouds were gathering again globally. But on Boxing Day 1938 she captured, vivaciously, just one aspect of that decade Crimson-lipped the cashier of the Ritz Dancing Hall in Manchester reflected the population's determination to find joy after the dark days of the First World War, the Great Depression, and unemployment The 1930s led novelist and broadcaster JB Priestley to his famous vision of "three Englands" – the ancient country of cathedrals and villages, the blackened and scarred industrial Britain created by the Victorians, and the Americanised new consumer world of suburbs, cinemas and m The decade in Britain saw a nation in transition. The north was hit hard by economic turmoil with unemployment levels soaring above the national average due to the collapse of industries like coal mining and shipbuilding However, seaside cities became alive in the 1930s, thanks to the expansion of cheap rail travel and the emerging concept of paid holidays with thousands of working-class families flooding to the coast during their “Wakes Weeks”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Everything heard in second week in the trial of a man accused of murdering Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins WARNING: Graphic details. Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering Michael Mullins View 9 Images Add to preferred sources New Simon Richardson, 35, struck Mr Mullins in his Volvo in Altrincham in April, at the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane, a jury was told. The 56-year-old was making his way home to Northwich from work, it was said It is alleged that Mr Richardson failed to properly observe the junction, 'flying straight through the give-way markers', before hitting Mr Mullins Minshull Street Crown Court heard that Mr Richardson 'put his foot down', as Mr Mullins was trapped under the car, while his damaged bike was left in the road He was dragged under the wheels of the car for 1.3 miles - 2.2km - before dying at the roadside on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm, it was said. Prosecutors allege that Mr Richardson later stopped, got out of the car and made 'concerted physical efforts' to try and pull Mr Mullins out from He then carried on driving, veering 'sharply and deliberately' from side to side and mounting a grass verge. Witnesses followed a trail of blood in the road before finding Mr Mullins fatally injured. He was pronounced dead at the scene

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester weather Roads blocked and thousands without power as Storm Boelo batters region for second day running Disruption was widespread on Sunday as gusts of up to 65mph hit Greater Manchester Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson S Greater Manchester was battered by wind and rain today (October 25) as Storm Boelo wreaked havoc on much of country the for a second day in a row Multiple flights were cancelled and 'do not travel' warnings issued as wind gusts of up to 65pm battered the region, which came under a yellow weather warning for wind, set to last until 9pm this evening Meanwhile a rest centre was set up at Ashton Leisure Centre in Ashton-in-Makerfield after damage to an electricity pole on Slag Lane left around 200 homes in the area without power The gusts brought down dozens of trees across the region, blocking roads in Cheadle , Gatley, Heaton Moor, Burnage, Wythenshawe , Moston , the A627 motorway in Oldham , and on a house in Stretford Trees also came down on multiple railway lines, including near Hadfield in Derbyshire, between Wigan and St Helens, and Manchester Piccadilly and Liverpool Lime Street stations

evidence_packet.lead: Councillor Pat Karney 'I couldn't deal with fire in my mouth': How losing his mum inspired Pat Karney's crusade to ban smoking Following the death of Cllr Pat Karney aged 78, John Scheerhout examines the personal tragedy that drove one of his greatest Add to preferred sources New
evidence_packet.summary: Councillor Pat Karney 'I couldn't deal with fire in my mouth': How losing his mum inspired Pat Karney's crusade to ban smoking Following the death of Cllr Pat Karney aged 78, John Scheerhout examines the personal tragedy that drove one of his greatest Add to preferred sources New
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Councillor Pat Karney 'I couldn't deal with fire in my mouth': How losing his mum inspired Pat Karney's crusade to ban smoking Following the death of Cllr Pat Karney aged 78, John Scheerhout examines the personal tragedy that drove one of his greatest Add to preferred sources News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 17:21, 25 Oct 2026 Updated 06:22, 26 Oct 2026 Pat Karney watched his beloved mother Mary die of smoking-related illness. The late Labour veteran possessed an ingrained sense of public duty but perhaps it was this intens For years before smoking in pubs and restaurants was eventually outlawed in England in 2007, he was the passionate leader for a campaign to make Manchester smoke-free. Of course, he believed his adopted home city of Manchester should always be first His late mother had been seduced into addiction by images of the glamorous Hollywood greats, puffing away on the silver screen. So in 2004 he resolved to do something about a public health crisis which was blighting Manchester more than anywhere else in the country He had tried smoking at London School of Economics where he got a BSc in politics and economics and even tried a joint on a trip to Amsterdam but disliked it immediately. He admitted he 'couldn't deal with having a fire in my mouth' His campaigning went through many ups and downs but ended in victory, and probably helped to save lives. He died earlier this month, aged 78

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Why Britain's top-performing police chief is being forced out - and his warning to the Home Office Following a leaked letter exposing a bitter rift with PCC Dan Price over his contract, retiring Cheshire Chief Constable Mark Roberts speaks to the M.E. Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 15:57, 25 Oct 2026 There is bit of old cross-county banter between Greater Manchester and Cheshire Police which Mark Roberts is familiar with. GMP would refer to their more rural neighbours as "The Gurkhas" - beca During his five and a half years tenure as Chief Constable of Cheshire Constabulary Roberts has made sure the joke is well and truly redundant The force is currently one of the best performing in the country according to His Majesty Inspectorate of Constabularies. A sweet fact for Roberts as his policing career began on the streets of Manchester and Salford This year Cheshire ranked top nationally for crime outcome rates, high charge/summons rates, and excellence in tackling violence, burglary, and sexual offences It therefore begs the question why after a 33-year stellar career he is choosing to retire early. He is due to leave the force on November 5th. But he had hoped to negotiate an extension to his contract which would have taken him to 2028

Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) 'have decided that replacement buses aren’t needed for the majority of stops,' they added It comes as three Metrolink lines are currently closed for a fortnight for engineering works on one of the busiest stretches of tram line in Europe. evidence_packet.lead: Councillor Pat Karney 'I couldn't deal with fire in my mouth': How losing his mum inspired Pat Karney's crusade to ban smoking Following the death of Cllr Pat Karney aged 78, John Scheerhout examines the personal tragedy that drove one of his greatest Add to preferred sources New
evidence_packet.summary: Councillor Pat Karney 'I couldn't deal with fire in my mouth': How losing his mum inspired Pat Karney's crusade to ban smoking Following the death of Cllr Pat Karney aged 78, John Scheerhout examines the personal tragedy that drove one of his greatest Add to preferred sources New
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Councillor Pat Karney 'I couldn't deal with fire in my mouth': How losing his mum inspired Pat Karney's crusade to ban smoking Following the death of Cllr Pat Karney aged 78, John Scheerhout examines the personal tragedy that drove one of his greatest Add to preferred sources News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 17:21, 25 Oct 2026 Updated 06:22, 26 Oct 2026 Pat Karney watched his beloved mother Mary die of smoking-related illness. The late Labour veteran possessed an ingrained sense of public duty but perhaps it was this intens For years before smoking in pubs and restaurants was eventually outlawed in England in 2007, he was the passionate leader for a campaign to make Manchester smoke-free. Of course, he believed his adopted home city of Manchester should always be first His late mother had been seduced into addiction by images of the glamorous Hollywood greats, puffing away on the silver screen. So in 2004 he resolved to do something about a public health crisis which was blighting Manchester more than anywhere else in the country He had tried smoking at London School of Economics where he got a BSc in politics and economics and even tried a joint on a trip to Amsterdam but disliked it immediately. He admitted he 'couldn't deal with having a fire in my mouth' His campaigning went through many ups and downs but ended in victory, and probably helped to save lives. He died earlier this month, aged 78

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mottram 'It’s torture. This is sleep deprivation. That is a recognised torture method' Former Tameside Mayor John Sullivan claims overnight M67 diversions for the £228m Mottram bypass project are sending 400 HGVs a night past his Hyde home - shaking b Add to preferred sources News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 17:56, 25 Oct 2026 Updated 06:21, 26 Oct 2026 Houses shake and residents are being kept up by lorries crashing over potholes in Mottram, according to one local John Sullivan says he’s not had a good night’s sleep since July, thanks to a diversion on the A57 link roads project. The scheme, also known as the Mottram bypass, has been designed to reduce congestion and improve journey times and reliability across the Pennines The A57 is a major connecting road between Manchester and Sheffield, which has been marred by congestion for years. The bypass was a ‘pie in the sky’ idea for more than 60 years, until spades finally went in the ground last year The current stage of roadworks is to allow the construction of a flyover from Hattersley roundabout to loop around Mottram village, go under Roe Cross, down to Mottram Moor and beyond towards Woolley Lane - ending at Woolley Bridge This progress on the scheme hasn’t made life easy for those that live nearby. John Sullivan lives just off the A57 Mottram Road in Hyde , where trans-Pennine lorries pass their homes through the night while it closes the M67 for roadworks

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Unseen pictures of 1930s from Manchester's Ritz to Rochdale 'Riviera' From Rochdale's lost "Norden Riviera" lido to an almost deserted East Lancashire Road, a remarkable new book featuring 600 unseen 1930s archive photographs captures Greater Manchest Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 05:53, 26 Oct 2026 Storm clouds were gathering again globally. But on Boxing Day 1938 she captured, vivaciously, just one aspect of that decade Crimson-lipped the cashier of the Ritz Dancing Hall in Manchester reflected the population's determination to find joy after the dark days of the First World War, the Great Depression, and unemployment The 1930s led novelist and broadcaster JB Priestley to his famous vision of "three Englands" – the ancient country of cathedrals and villages, the blackened and scarred industrial Britain created by the Victorians, and the Americanised new consumer world of suburbs, cinemas and m The decade in Britain saw a nation in transition. The north was hit hard by economic turmoil with unemployment levels soaring above the national average due to the collapse of industries like coal mining and shipbuilding However, seaside cities became alive in the 1930s, thanks to the expansion of cheap rail travel and the emerging concept of paid holidays with thousands of working-class families flooding to the coast during their “Wakes Weeks”

Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering Michael Mullins View 9 Images Add to preferred sources New Simon Richardson, 35, struck
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Everything heard in second week in the trial of a man accused of murdering Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins WARNING: Graphic details. Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering Michael Mullins View 9 Images Add to preferred sources New Simon Richardson, 35, struck Mr Mullins in his Volvo in Altrincham in April, at the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane, a jury was told. The 56-year-old was making his way home to Northwich from work, it was said It is alleged that Mr Richardson failed to properly observe the junction, 'flying straight through the give-way markers', before hitting Mr Mullins Minshull Street Crown Court heard that Mr Richardson 'put his foot down', as Mr Mullins was trapped under the car, while his damaged bike was left in the road He was dragged under the wheels of the car for 1.3 miles - 2.2km - before dying at the roadside on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm, it was said. Prosecutors allege that Mr Richardson later stopped, got out of the car and made 'concerted physical efforts' to try and pull Mr Mullins out from He then carried on driving, veering 'sharply and deliberately' from side to side and mounting a grass verge. Witnesses followed a trail of blood in the road before finding Mr Mullins fatally injured. He was pronounced dead at the scene

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester weather Roads blocked and thousands without power as Storm Boelo batters region for second day running Disruption was widespread on Sunday as gusts of up to 65mph hit Greater Manchester Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson S Greater Manchester was battered by wind and rain today (October 25) as Storm Boelo wreaked havoc on much of country the for a second day in a row Multiple flights were cancelled and 'do not travel' warnings issued as wind gusts of up to 65pm battered the region, which came under a yellow weather warning for wind, set to last until 9pm this evening Meanwhile a rest centre was set up at Ashton Leisure Centre in Ashton-in-Makerfield after damage to an electricity pole on Slag Lane left around 200 homes in the area without power The gusts brought down dozens of trees across the region, blocking roads in Cheadle , Gatley, Heaton Moor, Burnage, Wythenshawe , Moston , the A627 motorway in Oldham , and on a house in Stretford Trees also came down on multiple railway lines, including near Hadfield in Derbyshire, between Wigan and St Helens, and Manchester Piccadilly and Liverpool Lime Street stations

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport ‘For years I was scared of flying, now I hop on planes from London to Edinburgh’ Mark Wein overcame his fear of flying, now he's going to help passengers at Manchester Airport thanks to easyJet View 4 Images (Image: easyJet press of Add to preferred sources News Liv Clarke Tourism writer 17:12, 25 Oct 2026 Many of us don't think twice about hopping on board a plane and flying somewhere. After all, we live in an age where it can be cheaper to fly than catch a train Yet for some the thought of sitting inside an aircraft fills them with dread. A fear of flying can result in people feeling anxious before, during and after their flight, or it can even result in them avoiding planes altogether, even if that means missing out on holidays, seeing But there is a way to get over this fear. A course led by easyJet seeks to help people overcome their fear of flying, giving them the confidence to get on a plane and travel the world. This November it will be available at Manchester Airport The easyJet Fearless Flyer Course runs programmes at airports across the country, providing participants with coping techniques and strategies, information on technical aspects and explanations of things you may experience like turbulence, noises and take off. It culminates in an View 4 Images Course director Mark Wein attends the courses himself (Image: easyJet press office)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Why Britain's top-performing police chief is being forced out - and his warning to the Home Office Following a leaked letter exposing a bitter rift with PCC Dan Price over his contract, retiring Cheshire Chief Constable Mark Roberts speaks to the M.E. Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 15:57, 25 Oct 2026 There is bit of old cross-county banter between Greater Manchester and Cheshire Police which Mark Roberts is familiar with. GMP would refer to their more rural neighbours as "The Gurkhas" - beca During his five and a half years tenure as Chief Constable of Cheshire Constabulary Roberts has made sure the joke is well and truly redundant The force is currently one of the best performing in the country according to His Majesty Inspectorate of Constabularies. A sweet fact for Roberts as his policing career began on the streets of Manchester and Salford This year Cheshire ranked top nationally for crime outcome rates, high charge/summons rates, and excellence in tackling violence, burglary, and sexual offences It therefore begs the question why after a 33-year stellar career he is choosing to retire early. He is due to leave the force on November 5th. But he had hoped to negotiate an extension to his contract which would have taken him to 2028

evidence_packet.title: Storm Boelo rest centre opened as hundreds of Greater Manchester homes without power
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester weather Storm Boelo rest centre opened as hundreds of Greater Manchester homes without power Engineers are working across the North West Add to preferred sources Comments News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 15:08, 25 Oct 2026 Updated 15:09 Homes have been left without
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester weather Storm Boelo rest centre opened as hundreds of Greater Manchester homes without power Engineers are working across the North West Add to preferred sources Comments News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 15:08, 25 Oct 2026 Updated 15:09 Homes have been left without
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester weather Storm Boelo rest centre opened as hundreds of Greater Manchester homes without power Engineers are working across the North West Add to preferred sources Comments News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 15:08, 25 Oct 2026 Updated 15:09 Homes have been left without power after an electric pole was severely damaged in Storm Boelo . Wigan council has set up a rest centre for anyone affected by a power cut this afternoon (October 25) The power cut, on Slag Lane, is affecting homes in the Lowton and Golborne areas. Wigan council says around 200 homes have been left without electricity as a result, while a tree has also come crashing down It comes as SP Electricity North West listed more than 160 power cuts across the North West as of 2.40pm - including 11 in Greater Manchester. A Wigan council spokesperson said: "Due to damage to an electric pole on Slag Lane, approximately 200 homes in the area are currently wit "A rest centre is being set up at Ashton Leisure Centre, Old Road, Ashton-in-Makerfield, WN4 9TP for anyone affected. We would ask anyone able to travel there independently to please do so. There is limited transport available for those who need it. If you do need a lift, please "A tree has also come down on Slag Lane and damaged a telephone pole, so this road will continue to be closed until repairs can be safely carried out. Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service, Electricity North West and council staff are on site."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: By Stephen Topping Senior reporter 13:38, 25 OCT 2026 Bookmark A fallen tree on tha A627(M) (Image: submitted) Trees have been falling across Greater Manchester as Storm Boelo leaves its mark . Police had to close a lane on the A627(M) motorway after trees fel And trains were grounded between Manchester Piccadilly and Liverpool Lime Street due to a tree on the railway line, which has since been removed. The storm is causing major disruption in Greater Manchester and beyond Roads across the region have been hit by fallen trees, while engineers are responding to several power cuts. In the worst affected areas of the North West, engineers are unable to carry out repairs as the wind remains strong The Met Office has a yellow weather warning for strong winds in force across Greater Manchester until 9pm tonight. The warning also covers the rest of northern England, Scotland and much of North Wales A more severe amber warning is in force further north, including parts of Lancashire. A more severe amber warning is also in force further north, including parts of Lancashire It comes after Storm Boelo has already brought downpours to the UK on Saturday, with further showers expected today. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Christie Hospital 'I always knew something was wrong - doctors told me it was just anxiety' After her symptoms were repeatedly dismissed as "just anxiety" for a decade before being diagnosed with incurable medullary thyroid cancer, 26-year-old Sas Add to preferred sources Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 07:21, 25 Oct 2026 A young woman living with a rare form of incurable cancer says she spent years being told her symptoms were "just anxiety" before finally receiving a diagnosis Saskia Clark, 26, said she was "always unwell" as a teenager, struggling with extreme tiredness and bowel issues. She repeatedly visited her GP but was often told her symptoms were due to anxiety or that she would "grow out of it" But two years ago, after a student doctor took a closer look at her symptoms and urgently referred her for a CT scan, Saskia was diagnosed with medullary thyroid cancer - a rare cancer that forms inside the thyroid gland Now, she undergoes scans every three months to monitor the disease and check whether her treatment is working. She is sharing her story to support an appeal by the Manchester Evening News and The Christie Charity to build a new scanning centre at The Christie in Manchester DONATE TO THE FUNDRAISER BY THE CHRISTIE CHARITY AND MANCHESTER EVENING NEWS HERE

title: 'You can see the terror in a kid's eyes when they wake up and can't breathe'

evidence_packet.title: 'You can see the terror in a kid's eyes when they wake up and can't breathe'
evidence_packet.lead: Health 'You can see the terror in a kid's eyes when they wake up and can't breathe' More than 20,000 kids were hospitalised for breathing issues in Greater Manchester last year View 4 Images (Image: PA) Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 07:16
evidence_packet.summary: Health 'You can see the terror in a kid's eyes when they wake up and can't breathe' More than 20,000 kids were hospitalised for breathing issues in Greater Manchester last year View 4 Images (Image: PA) Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 07:16
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Health 'You can see the terror in a kid's eyes when they wake up and can't breathe' More than 20,000 kids were hospitalised for breathing issues in Greater Manchester last year View 4 Images (Image: PA) Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 07:16, 25 Oct 2026 Dessie was five years old the first time he woke up in the middle of the night, unable to breathe “It was really scary,” his mum, Hilary Judd, 49, said. “He woke up and was crying and panicking, which was making it even harder for him to breathe. You could see the terror in a kid's eyes when they wake up and they can't breathe but they don't really understand what’s going on. Dessie, now eight, suffers from severe asthma. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Council is one of at least four local authorities who have refused to accept the government's latest planning changes. Credit: PNW Four local authorities have drawn lines in the sand, refusing to amend their constitutions to adopt the latest statutory government guidance that would see officers become the default body for deciding most planning applications across England Bolton Council, Tameside Council, Central Bedfordshire Council, and Fenland Council have refused to amend their constitutions to be compliant with the National Scheme of Delegation of Planning Functions, which goes into effect on 1 November Their decision will inevitably have consequences, should they continue to refuse to comply In short, the regulation changes mean that more applications will be decided by officers and less by committees This will create a national standard for what is, and what is not, taken to council planning committees – whereas previously local authorities could set their own guidelines for what sort of application merited the committee treatment

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Acumen Waste Service Limited have started preparatory works to remove the illegally deposited waste at Bolton House Road Following a robust tender process, Wigan Council announced that it had chosen Acumen as its preferred contractor last month, with contracts now officially signed after a compulsory standstill period Acumen is bringing in equipment and clearing vegetation at the Bickershaw site to allow waste to start being removed in the coming weeks Councillor Nazia Rehman, Leader of Wigan Council, said: “The contract signing and mobilisation at Bolton House Road is a clear sign of progress and a significant moment for the community who have had to deal with the impact of the illegal waste site “Reaching this stage also demonstrates the commitment of the council and partners to deliver the necessary framework for waste clearance, but our work does not stop here “We will continue to work with residents to ensure their voice is heard in the future of the site and will continue to support the Environment Agency’s criminal investigation to make sure those responsible are held accountable for the damage and distress they have caused.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Council is introducing new orders to tackle anti-social behaviour in Wigan and Leigh town centres, including targeted powers against e-bikes and scooters These Public Space Protection Orders (PSPOs) will be in place for three years to support the police, council and other authorities in tackling a wide range of issues, reduce crime and help people feel safer in their communities This introduction follows an extensive review of previous orders and a public consultation held over the summer which gathered significant feedback from residents, businesses and the community sector Councillor Kevin Anderson, cabinet portfolio holder for Police, Crime and Civil Contingencies, said: “Residents, businesses and visitors all took part in our consultation, and it was clear that anti-social behaviour remains a concern “Most people who visit, live and work in our town centres do so responsibly, and these orders are aimed at addressing the small number of behaviours that negatively impact our communities, while ensuring support remains available for those who may be vulnerable.” The orders prohibit several anti-social behaviours, with new powers to enforce against anti-social use of cycles, e-bikes and scooters, and drug-related litter and paraphernalia

evidence_packet.evidence_text: We know residents have questions about the future of Gibfield and recent activity around the site. This update explains the current position, what survey activity means and how local people can take part in any future planning process In August 2026, Wigan Council’s Cabinet agreed to object to Peel Land’s proposed Gibfield Park masterplan. Cabinet’s position was that the housing and industrial proposals were not acceptable in their current form and did not have cabinet members’ support. No planning application West of Gibfield was allocated for homes, employment and green space through Places for Everyone, which was adopted in 2024 and now forms part of the statutory development plan. The current Wigan Local Plan process cannot reverse that allocation. However, allocation does not gran Our chief executive has written to the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, requesting Gibfield to be removed from the plan. We are waiting for a response Cabinet has formally objected to the proposed masterplan and made clear that it cannot support the development now or in the future Peel Land may undertake ecology surveys, ground-condition testing, environmental work and traffic or transport studies to understand the site and prepare evidence. These investigations do not mean planning permission has been granted or that a future application will be approved

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.summary: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

evidence_packet.evidence_text: L-R: Simon Shaw, Anna Dick, Alastair Brown, Tripti Anil, Alan Jackson Simon Shaw, Delivery Director at Codurance, hosted the lunchtime session for tech leaders and introduced Codurance, which is a global software engineering consultancy that has run its Manchester office for 15 years He was joined on the panel by Anna Dick, Chief Technology & Product Officer at Capsule; Alastair Brown, Group Director of AI and Technology at Peninsula; Tripti Anil, Senior Leader, Data & Analytics at Kellanova; and Alan Jackson, Director of Client Solutions at Codurance Talking about discovering how AI can be used in projects, Anna said that Capsule's initial three months of AI exploration across all its business teams built appetite for further experimentation, but it also got a little out of control. evidence_packet.summary: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, back
evidence_packet.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A new exhibition at The Portico Library explores feminist themes of wellbeing, ageing and place in relation to magic and ritual healing Open now, Witches & Healers draws on Rosie Reed Hillman’s groundbreaking project Something That Was Ours , which explores what it means to be a witch today Hillman’s portraits of witches and healers are curated in dialogue with historic texts chosen by critical friends who identify with the practice of witchcraft and/or healing. The portraits, the books chosen, and their interpretation offer unique insights into the diverse lives an Using a mix of moving image and photography, the artwork builds a sensory and emotive portrait of women in midlife. Covering themes of menopause, mental health, climate change, and marital breakdown, this work explores the ways women have reclaimed the word witch and sought solac Speaking about the exhibition , Rosie Reed Hillman says: “I have worked to build rapport with contributors over the last four years and believe the intimate access conveyed in this project creates an exhibition that inspires empathy, curiosity and a greater understanding of issue “Women in midlife of all backgrounds are an overlooked demographic who want to see art and hear stories that reflect their experiences, and I hope this work speaks to them especially.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.title: Why Cole Palmer is not suspended for Chelsea vs Man United after Tottenham red card
evidence_packet.lead: Cole Palmer is available to play for Chelsea against Manchester United in the Premier League at Stamford Bridge despite being sent off against Tottenham Hotspur
evidence_packet.summary: Cole Palmer is available to play for Chelsea against Manchester United in the Premier League at Stamford Bridge despite being sent off against Tottenham Hotspur
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC Why Cole Palmer is not suspended for Chelsea vs Man United after Tottenham red card Cole Palmer is available to play for Chelsea against Manchester United in the Premier League at Stamford Bridge despite being sent off against Tottenham Hotspur Manchester United will still have to face Cole Palmer when they play Chelsea in the Premier League at Old Trafford on Halloween Palmer was sent off in their 2-0 defeat to Tottenham Hotspur after being issued two yellow cards within the space of nine second-half minutes. Such a red card results in an automatic one-match suspension, with United being the Blues' next league opponents, but that is not their n Chelsea are still in the Carabao Cup and play their fourth-round tie against Liverpool at Anfield this midweek. Therefore, that is the match Palmer will be suspended for The suspensions from red cards issued in the Premier League also apply to matches in both domestic cup competitions and vice versa. Only bans due to yellow card accumulation are limited to league games, as they are in UEFA competitions Xabi Alonso could conceivably have rested Palmer in midweek anyway. The Chelsea head coach did so by naming his player among the substitutes in their third-round tie against Leeds United
